title: Excellent for beginners, but completely locks out advanced English speakers
text:
I purchased a lifetime subscription to Mondly because my education and first language is English, and I wanted to use the app to master Advanced English. Unfortunately, the app has a major technical limitation: it does not allow a user to select English for both the native ("I speak") and target ("I want to learn") languages.
Because I cannot read the Hindi script easily, setting my native language to Hindi doesn't work for me. Trying a workaround by setting my native language to Spanish or French just means I cannot understand the instructions.
Mondly needs to allow English-to-English learning for advanced students who want to refine their fluency. The app is fantastic for learning a brand-new language from scratch using English instructions, but it is currently useless for fluent speakers trying to access the Advanced English course. I hope the developers fix this restriction soon.

title: Please fix past/present/future pop-up and add feature
text: Fix this and I’ll give you a 4: when you tap a word to see its grammar breakdown, the tense selector defaults to “Present,” but the example text shown is actually past tense — the label doesn’t match the content. Add this and I’ll give you a 5: on-demand AI grammar lessons, so there’s always an AI tutor available to explain the “why” behind things, not just show examples. Like why certain endings exist — in Spanish, “-ían” endings work like “-ing” does in English for ongoing past actions — or why you can drop “nosotros” since the “-mos” ending already means “we.” Basically, let users ask about any grammar point they’re curious about and get a real explanation, not just more drills.

title: I enjoy this app but
text:
I get frustrated when I get an answer wrong and then can't fix it. I just want to learn, not feel bad about myself.

Also, some of the Japanese words that are used are not commonly used in casual conversations. Like when you are talking about yourself you don't have to start the sentence with watashiwa. Also, starting a sentence with "anatawa", I've read, is viewed as cold, or even rude. Another word that gets used in the app that probably shouldn't be is chiketto (ticket). I've studied Japanese for a while now and I've never heard that word used before. I've only heard the word "kippu" as the Japanese word to use for "ticket". Other than the above, I do enjoy using this app.

9/2/26: I think it's ridiculous that I can get answers in English wrong. You have to fix that. The answer I chose was "I find homework stimulating." The "correct" answer was "I find homework to be stimulating." Give me a break. Both sentences mean the same thing. title: Frustrating at times
text:
The app seems okay, I like that it offers many languages. The lessons are all over the place and could be better organized and more flexible.  Mondly could also easily offer lesson plans based on the users goal.  I am learning for travel yet I end up sifting through unrelated and generally unhelpful content.  Having focused learning plans seems like it would be pretty easy and would make the app so much better.  

The app is frustrating at times with its speech recognition, or lack of.  I’ve recorded the app saying a word and played the recorded back and the app won’t recognize the word.  The deeper I get the more I run into words the AI simply won’t pick up on.  This wastes time and is frustrating.  

There is also a real lack of conversational content that’s not scripted.  I’ve downloaded a second app for that.  

This app seems like it has a good start but it’s also really lacking essential features.  Better than Duolingo but then what’s not?

title: Decent but needs some work
text:
I’ve been using this app for several months to learn Dutch & my experience has been fine for the most part but there are some areas that need work. 

-Different difficulty levels (Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced) do not add more complex sentences nor additional verbs, different verb tenses or much of anything else that would aid you in advancing your knowledge of the language. Practice vocabulary and sentences throughout all difficulty levels are almost all EXACTLY the same, with a few new ones thrown in sporadically. The speech practice at the end of each category is exactly the same throughout all levels, no changes or increased difficulty & they’re already marked as completed when moving through the different knowledge levels. There a few noticeable differences: beginner levels - practice 2 words/sentences, then quiz. Intermediate levels - practice 4-5 words/sentences, then quiz. Advanced levels -  practice 5+ words/sentences, then quiz. But the words/sentences are the same throughout all levels.

-The tool used to grade speech practice can be frustrating to use & is, at times, highly inconsistent. What it judges as what was said versus what was actually said can be way off. Sometimes what it hears is nothing close to what was said. Sometimes it doesn’t matter what was said, it judges it to be wrong. It will decide that you’ve said one thing & every answer given after that (even if a completely different thing is said) is that first incorrect word & nothing will change it. Sometimes it will count something spoken correctly as wrong but the audio guide will say correct & move on. Sometimes it will judge that you mispronounced a word regardless of how many times you try to change your pronunciation but when the same word is spoken in a sentence, it marks it as correct or vice versa. Another issue I’ve run into is that it switches written out numbers to digits & then will count them wrong. As an example, if you’re meant to say fifteen, it will show that you said 15 & count it wrong. The same goes for currency. Euro will be displayed as € and counted as wrong. I’ve messaged about this issue to the developers & it seemed to be fixed but just finished a speaking lesson where this issue occurred again. 

-In general the app is better than other language apps that I’ve previously used but there are some areas that really do need improving. The provided sentences would actually be useful in real life situations but would need more in order to expand beyond general tourist level fluency of the language.

title: Bad methods and inconsistent technology
text:
I have 3 core problems:
1. Voice recording and recognition for pronunciation practice is bad. I frequently can’t get it to record something even close to what I said. Also, the desktop browser app won’t even recognize my mic. 
2. It’s fine for words and short phrases, but for any longer phrases with more complex sentence structure or verb conjugations, it does nothing to explain these differences. I don’t know what the grammar is. I can’t easily match up words to words so I know the individual words in the phrase instead of just the whole thing verbatim, which isn’t effective at helping me remember. And if the verb it uses is a different form or conjugation from what it has taught or has in the reference, it does not explain this at all. So I frequently can’t even identify the verb in the sentence and I don’t know why it’s different or when to use it. 
3. This lack of explanation is made into a bigger problem because the exercises and tests are super easy and built in a way that doesn’t require you remember things or understand anything to pass them. For example: You are given 2 words with pictures of what they are and a word in English to match to one of the two other words… which you have pictures for, so you don’t even need to know the word. Another example: An exercise where you are given a phrase to translate and either a set of answer phrases or a collection of words to create the sentence. Except that there will be so few answers and the wrong answers will have something obviously, structurally wrong with them that lets you eliminate them without thinking about it. For example you’re given a question but only one answer is a question. Or a phrase with capitalization and only one phrase has a capital. So I find myself completing these only to realize that I don’t actually remember what I “learned.” 

I’m glad that I was diligent about trying the app deep enough into the lessons before the trial had ended. If I had only done the first few lessons I might not have realized just how useless this is.
